title: Understanding Bias and Variance
text: When we talk about bias in a model, we're referring to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. Variance, on the other hand, refers to the model's sensitivity to fluctuations in the training data. If the bias decreases, what might that imply about the model's complexity?

title: Exploring Model Complexity
text: If the model bias decreased, which of the following could be true about the model's complexity?
choices: The model complexity stayed the same.

title: Linking Bias and Variance
text: Consider how changes in model complexity might affect both bias and variance. If a model becomes more complex, what typically happens to its variance?

title: Impact on Variance
text: If the model complexity increased, what is likely to happen to the model's variance?
choices: The model variance stayed the same.
